reason: The expression variable polyfill treated ArrowFunctionExpression as 'do nothing', so a concise arrow body that is a bare identifier (() => process) was never routed through the data context and reached host globals, escaping the expression sandbox into command execution.

kbc.notes: Fix commit is the 'Bundle/2.x' release-branch commit #34680 (n8n ships security fixes in bundle commits; the file diff isolates this sink). Fixed 2.31.5/2.32.1. First of an expression-sandbox chain: GHSA-hw8v and GHSA-6xcw (2026-09) are later bypasses of the same sandbox with different holes.

reason: PrototypeSanitizer visited assignments and member access but had no visitClassBody, so a class field with a reserved name (or a template-literal key) rebound the sanitizer's own reserved variables and the expression escaped the sandbox to code execution.

kbc.notes: Bundle 2.x commit #37586 (fixed 2.38.2/2.37.7/1.123.76). Incomplete-fix chain: a further bypass of the hardening after kbc-ghsa-gv7g-jm28-cr3m. Locator is the visitor list where visitClassBody was missing.

reason: The code printer emitted identifier names through recast's literal printer and JSON.stringify at print time; tampering with shared builtins (JSON.stringify) or crafting names injected source into the generated 'name in data ? data : global' switch, executing attacker code outside the sandbox.

kbc.notes: Same bundle commit as kbc-ghsa-hw8v-xxg5-vvvx but a different file and sink (code-printer injection; fix adds rawStringLiteral and safeStringify captured at load).

reason: The XML node validated a coerced copy (String(options.attrkey)) against __proto__/constructor/prototype but passed the original, non-string option value on to xml2js, so a crafted array value bypassed the earlier prototype-pollution fix and polluted Object.prototype.

kbc.notes: Patch bypass (incomplete fix) of GHSA-hqr4-h3xv-9m3r; the fix validates the value that is actually used. Bundle 2.x commit #30359. rd_class sandbox-escape is the closest enum value for prototype-pollution-to-RCE.

reason: The Python task-runner AST validator blocked dangerous attributes and regex-checked literal format strings, but allowed bare str.format / format_map attribute access and aliasing, so format-string attribute traversal reached blocked internals and escaped the Python sandbox.

kbc.notes: Bundle 2.x commit #31173 (fixed 2.22.4/2.21.8/1.123.48); the fix adds bare-format attribute rejection in the validator and a FormatGuardTransformer in the executor.

reason: The Git node's clone validated the target path and then cloned into it later, so swapping a directory for a symlink between check and use (TOCTOU) planted a repo in the community-nodes directory, which n8n loads as code on the next restart.

kbc.notes: Bundle 2.x commit #33793 (fixed 2.30.1). Fix clones into an unguessable staging dir and renames into place. Part of the Git-node incomplete-fix history (GHSA-57g9, GHSA-rcv6 not pinned, see notes file).

reason: ContextExpression substituted string ContextVariable values into the expression with a raw f-string (no repr/escaping) and then eval()ed it; the AST allow-list ran on the template, not on the substituted expression, so a quote in any variable value breaks out into arbitrary Python.

kbc.notes: Fixed in 0.13.2. The commit message cites GHSA-9fvw-gr53-m7fw (not resolvable via the API); repo advisory 35w5 describes the same eval sink. Variable values arrive from tool output, APIs or persisted state, hence untrusted-data-store.

reason: DiskKnowledgeStore confined virtual paths with str.startswith on the resolved root, so a sibling directory sharing the root's name prefix (/data/root-evil vs /data/root) passed the containment check.

kbc.notes: Classic startswith-prefix containment bug; the fix is Path.is_relative_to. Fixed 1.1.0.

reason: Skill archive installation joined tar member names onto the staging dir without checking the result stayed inside it and used the archive-supplied skill name as a path before validating it, enabling arbitrary file write and (via rmtree of final_dest) delete.

kbc.notes: Fixed 1.1.0. Two sinks in one function (write at line 99, rmtree before validation ~118); one row, the extraction write.

reason: SandboxShellTool's restricted mode rejected shell operators from a denylist that omitted newline and carriage return, so 'allowed_cmd\nrm -rf ...' passed the allowed=[...] / readonly=True prefix check and the second line ran as a command.

kbc.notes: CVE-2026-113663, fixed 1.1.1. Allowlist/denylist bypass in an agent shell tool. Follow-up bef9a8efc0 (1.1.2, GHSA-42mf) reworks the filter again: deferred.

reason: Resource-scoped auth decorators (@auth.on.threads(actions=[...])) ignored actions= and always registered the handler for '*', so a narrow handler shadowed the broader fallback handler that enforced ownership and the authorization check never ran for other actions.

kbc.notes: Fixed in langgraph-sdk 0.4.4. Design-level authz bug in the framework's own auth API (the application code is correct as written).

reason: Inspector's connection settings (transport, serverCommand, serverArgs) were read from window.location on every route including /oauth/callback, so a malicious MCP server's OAuth redirect to the callback with transport=stdio&serverCommand=... switched Inspector to stdio and ran an arbitrary local command.

kbc.notes: v1 line fix (1.0.3). OAuth-callback confused-deputy into stdio exec; fix ignores query params on /oauth/callback.

reason: A remote MCP App's ui/open-link request made the client window.open() an attacker URL without noopener, giving the page a handle/sessionStorage access to steal the proxy auth token; because the sandbox is same-origin with the proxy, the missing-Origin check let it then call the stdio launch API (RCE).

kbc.notes: v1 line fix (1.0.3). Same commit adds a Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin refusal in server/src/index.ts originValidationMiddleware; locator is the noopener/open-link step of the chain.

reason: Origin validation only rejected a present-but-wrong Origin; with DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH set, a request with no Origin (any non-browser client) reached the privileged stdio launch route without a token, re-opening CVE-2025-49596.

kbc.notes: Incomplete-fix chain: bypass of kbc-ghsa-7f8r-222p-6f5g (v1 line, fixed 1.0.3). Fix also makes DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH parse strictly (true/1/yes).

reason: Inspector opened the OAuth authorization_endpoint chosen by the remote MCP server via npm open v10, which on Windows/WSL embeds the URL in a PowerShell double-quoted string, so a $(...) subexpression in the URL executes code while connecting.

kbc.notes: v2 line fix 2.12.0 (bump open to v11, restrict to http(s)). Follow-up f7e0377ab8 opens the serialized URL rather than the raw input. Same sink class as kbc-ghsa-6xpm-ggf7-wc3p (mcp-remote).

reason: The web server served index.html with the API token injected on routes outside the /api origin check and never validated the Host header, so a DNS-rebinding page could fetch / same-origin (no Origin header), read the token and then the stored OAuth secrets.

kbc.notes: Incomplete-fix chain: second bypass of CVE-2025-49596 (v2 line, fixed 2.12.0); fix adds a Host allow-list on every request.

reason: OAuthProxy.authorize() redirected straight to the upstream IdP for any dynamically registered client with no user consent step, so an attacker's client could ride the victim's existing IdP session (confused-deputy account takeover).

kbc.notes: Fix #2056 'Prevent confused deputy attacks in OAuth proxy' adds the consent screen, CSRF token and redirect-URI warnings. Confused-deputy chain, 1 of 2: consent added here, bypassed by kbc-ghsa-rww4-4w9c-7733 (consent not bound to the browser at the IdP callback).

reason: _handle_idp_callback loaded the transaction and issued the client authorization code without checking that the browser arriving at the callback is the one that approved consent; a lured victim whose IdP skips its own consent page completes the attacker's flow.

kbc.notes: Incomplete-fix chain, 2 of 2 (bypass of the consent screen from kbc-ghsa-c2jp-c369-7pvx). Fix #3201 adds a signed consent-binding cookie verified in the callback. A follow-up CSRF double-submit fix is #3519 (8fdb3cc2). VARIANT seed: consent/state bound to the flow but not to the browser.

reason: OAuthProxy issued its own JWTs with a fixed audience derived from base_url and ignored the RFC 8707 `resource` parameter, so a token minted for one MCP server is valid at any other server sharing the proxy's keys/base URL (token reuse across MCP servers).

kbc.notes: Fix #2764 builds the JWTIssuer in set_mcp_path() with the real resource URL and validates the client's `resource`. Audience-binding class (MCP spec token passthrough).

reason: open_repo validated only the textual repo_path against --repository, then git.Repo(path) followed a nested .git file (gitdir: /outside) so every tool operated on a repository outside the allowed one.

kbc.notes: Confinement chain, 1 of 2. Fix adds validate_opened_repo (checks git-dir, common-dir and worktree git actually uses); merged via PR #5333 (b711f8d3). Bypassed by kbc-ghsa-q74p-4wrc-q7w6.

reason: validate_opened_repo (the fix for GHSA-w766) accepted any git dir that equalled the allowed repo's own and ignored objects/info/alternates and linked-worktree git dirs, so an in-repo repository could still read objects from outside --repository.

kbc.notes: Confinement chain, 2 of 2: incomplete fix of kbc-ghsa-w766-5x43-whvw. Same commit a4a43ac fixes GHSA-6hqx (separate row, different sink). Merged by PR #5514 (1629bb33).

reason: Every tool opened the repository and ran git against it with the repository's own .git/config trusted, so core.fsmonitor, hooks, filter drivers, gpg.program etc. in a cloned/unpacked repo run arbitrary programs as the server user even on read-only calls such as git_status.

kbc.notes: Config-exec wave, 1 of 6 (head of chain). Fix adds harden_repo(): GIT_CONFIG_COUNT overrides + per-repo driver blanking. The five rows below are bypasses of this hardening. Pattern: git wrapper that does not neutralise repository-controlled config.

reason: The driver-listing regex needed at least one character in the driver name (filter\..+\.), so a driver with an empty name ([filter ""] clean = ...) was never blanked and still ran a program.

kbc.notes: Config-exec wave, 2 of 6: bypass of the harden_repo fix (kbc-ghsa-6hqx-gqrx-c5r2). Vuln SHA e1d154ee is shared by the 11-18 bypass rows (pm7p, 87qg, h2g3, 9vjp, 8wv7); locators differ. The fixes are stacked branches v2/fix/ghsa-*, each advisory with its own commit.

reason: harden_repo did not stop lazy fetching: a repository with promisor-remote configuration made git fetch missing objects, and the fetch ran a program the config names.

kbc.notes: Config-exec wave, 3 of 6: fix sets GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 and refuses promisor remotes on older git.

reason: git_merge could trigger automatic maintenance (git gc --auto), which honours gc.recentObjectsHook from the repository's own config and runs it; HARDENED_CONFIG did not disable maintenance.auto / gc.auto.

kbc.notes: Config-exec wave, 4 of 6: fix adds maintenance.auto=false and gc.auto=0 to HARDENED_CONFIG. The locator is the hardening list that lacks the entry.

reason: harden_repo read the repository config once, but git_merge writes the working tree: a merged branch can add a file that a config [include] now pulls in, defining filter/merge drivers that were never blanked and then run on the next git command.

kbc.notes: Config-exec wave, 5 of 6: fix routes every tree-writing command through _rewrite_tree(), which re-runs harden_repo afterwards. TOCTOU on hardened config.

reason: harden_repo only blanked filter/merge drivers from the top repository's config; a checked-out submodule's own config and .gitattributes still selected a driver that ran during git_add/git_checkout/git_diff.

kbc.notes: Config-exec wave, 6 of 6: fix adds _submodule_drivers() and diff.submodule=short; two follow-up commits complete it.
